fields.name: Top-Up Grind (g)
fields.description: Additional coffee ground after the initial timed grind to bring final basket dose closer to target. Positive number only. Used for correction analysis and bean usage if it represents additional coffee leaving the hopper.

fields.name: Over Grind Removed (g)
fields.description: Positive amount removed from the output because the grind produced more coffee than target dose. Informational only; do not add this to Bean Delta because it is already included in grinder output.

fields.name: Grind Waste (g)
fields.description: Positive amount of coffee intentionally removed during purge, cleanout, bag transition, or grinder emptying. This represents additional coffee leaving the hopper and should affect Bean Delta.

fields.name: Beans Added (g)
fields.description: I always add 300 grams of beans to make for a consistent pattern unless at beginning or end of bag. Beginning I fill grinder channel, grind and top off. End of bag I put in remaining beans and use that selector till hopper empties out.

fields.name: Hopper Fullness
fields.description: Percent estimate of total beans remaining in the grinder hopper system, including both the visible upper hopper and the lower funnel/throat area above the burrs. Important calibration note for the Eureka Magnifico: about 25 g of beans can remain below the cutoff slider, so the visible hopper reaching the cutoff slider does not mean near-empty. Log Hopper Fullness by total remaining bean mass impression, not just visible bean height in the upper chamber. Operational guide: 100% = freshly filled reference level; 75% = clearly above midpoint with strong column weight; 50% = about half of total usable bean mass remains; 30% = low-fill zone where column weight is reduced but meaningful bean mass still remains; 15% = very low visible fill, but still may include the lower hidden reserve below the cutoff slider; 0% = hopper intentionally emptied or effectively out of beans.

fields.name: Hopper Range
fields.description: Categorizes hopper fullness into percentage ranges based on decimal values.
